_meta.title: Strategy ledger and leaderboard
_meta.competition_rule: A strategy is ranked by gates passed, then by ROI. Ranking is cosmetic: no reward is payable unless status is VALIDATED.
_meta.headline_finding: Zero of eight strategies are validated. The binding constraint is sample size: the largest graded set is 14 bets against a floor of 100. This is reported as the result, not worked around.
_meta.reward_policy: Rewards are only payable to VALIDATED strategies. Because none are validated, the current reward allocation is zero and the leaderboard is informational only.
_meta.sample_note: The 14 graded games are also look-ahead contaminated (see backtest.py). Even the numerical hit rates are inflated and are not evidence of skill.
_meta.grading_convention: Wins pay +100/110 units, losses pay -1 unit. No sportsbook price was observable in this environment, so the standard -110 price is assumed and disclosed rather than presented as observed.
_meta.gates_are_not_all_equally_strong: G3 (bootstrap), G4 (stability) and G5 (fragility) are all satisfiable by luck when n is tiny. The NULL CONTROL demonstrates this: a coin-flip strategy passed 4 of 6 gates on these 14 games. The only gates that cannot be gamed at small n are G1 (sample floor) and G2 (Bonferroni-corrected significance), which is precisely why G1 is the first gate. A reader should treat any 'gates passed' count below 6 as meaningless — the conjunction is what matters.
_meta.bonferroni_note: 8 strategies were tested in this batch, so every p-value is multiplied by 8 before comparison with 0.05.

leaderboard.name: High-confidence moneyline

G2_significance.requirement: one-sided binomial p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction

G5_fragility.requirement: still profitable after removing the best 5% of bets

G6_provenance.requirement: every driving input from an approved official host
G6_provenance.note: Inputs are the NBA.com team ratings and official final scores; all pass.

leaderboard.rule: Bet the model's pick straight up when its win probability is at least 0.65.
leaderboard.why_it_might_work: A large rating gap is the only signal the model has that is not noise-dominated at n=14. If the model has any real information, it shows up here first.

leaderboard.rule: Bet the model's pick straight up when its win probability is at least 0.75.
leaderboard.why_it_might_work: A stricter cut than S01: fewer bets, larger gaps, less noise per bet but far fewer observations.

leaderboard.name: NULL CONTROL — coin flip

G2_significance.requirement: one-sided binomial p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction

G5_fragility.requirement: still profitable after removing the best 5% of bets

G6_provenance.requirement: every driving input from an approved official host
G6_provenance.note: Inputs are the NBA.com team ratings and official final scores; all pass.

leaderboard.rule: Bet a coin flip on every game in the backtest sample.
leaderboard.why_it_might_work: It cannot. It exists to prove the gates reject noise, so a passing grade elsewhere means something.

leaderboard.name: Total deviation fade

G2_significance.requirement: one-sided binomial p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction

G5_fragility.requirement: still profitable after removing the best 5% of bets

G6_provenance.requirement: every driving input from an approved official host
G6_provenance.note: Inputs are the NBA.com team ratings and official final scores; all pass.

leaderboard.rule: When the model's projected total sits more than 6 points away from the league-average total, take that side of the baseline and grade against the realised total.
leaderboard.why_it_might_work: Pace drives totals with r=0.79 across teams, so a large projected deviation is the model's most defensible claim.

leaderboard.name: Two-leg moneyline parlay, cross-game

G2_significance.requirement: one-sided binomial p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction

G5_fragility.requirement: still profitable after removing the best 5% of bets

G6_provenance.requirement: every driving input from an approved official host
G6_provenance.note: Inputs are the NBA.com team ratings and official final scores; all pass.

leaderboard.blocking_reason: No slate produced two picks at the required confidence with both games finished. Cross-game leg correlation is also unmeasured (correlations.json tier C), so the independence assumption behind the parlay price would itself be unverified.
leaderboard.rule: Combine the two highest-confidence moneyline picks on a slate.
leaderboard.why_it_might_work: If leg win probabilities are informative, compounding two of them raises the payout faster than it raises the variance.

leaderboard.name: Player prop over, half-line

G2_significance.requirement: one-sided binomial p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction

G5_fragility.requirement: still profitable after removing the best 5% of bets

G6_provenance.requirement: every driving input from an approved official host
G6_provenance.note: Inputs are the NBA.com team ratings and official final scores; all pass.

leaderboard.blocking_reason: The per-game sigma used for props is a modelled estimate, not a measured distribution, and no finished prop outcomes were captured to grade against. Grading without real outcomes is impossible, so this stays ungraded.
leaderboard.rule: Take the over on a player prop line set half a point below his season average, when the normal-approximation probability clears 0.55.
leaderboard.why_it_might_work: Season-average anchoring with a half-line buffer avoids pushes, and the prop lines are derived from the same verified player table.

leaderboard.name: Same-game parlay: player points + team total

G2_significance.requirement: one-sided binomial p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction

G5_fragility.requirement: still profitable after removing the best 5% of bets

G6_provenance.requirement: every driving input from an approved official host
G6_provenance.note: Inputs are the NBA.com team ratings and official final scores; all pass.

leaderboard.blocking_reason: This is exactly the correlation that could not be measured (correlations.json tier C). Without the joint distribution, the parlay price is a guess, so the strategy cannot be validated — only asserted. Left ungraded deliberately.
leaderboard.rule: Pair a player-points over with the same game's total over.
leaderboard.why_it_might_work: Both legs lean on pace, so the combination could be positively correlated in a way a book might under-price.

leaderboard.name: Injury-fade total under

G2_significance.requirement: one-sided binomial p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction

G5_fragility.requirement: still profitable after removing the best 5% of bets

G6_provenance.requirement: every driving input from an approved official host
G6_provenance.note: Inputs are the NBA.com team ratings and official final scores; all pass.

leaderboard.blocking_reason: The first qualifying games (CLE@MIA, GSW@SAS on 11/13) have not been played. No outcome exists to grade.
leaderboard.rule: Take the under when a NEW absence removes at least 12 expected points from one side.
leaderboard.why_it_might_work: A genuinely new absence is information the season-long ratings cannot contain, which is the one place the model can beat a rating-only baseline.

what_would_unblock_each_strategy.need: At least 100 completed games with pre-game ratings captured before tip-off, so no look-ahead bias.
Same, plus point-in-time totals so the deviation is not measured against the game it is predicting.
A licensed two-sided price to parlay against, and a measured cross-game correlation.
Per-game player logs to estimate sigma empirically, plus recorded prop outcomes.
The joint player-points/game-total distribution (correlations tier C).
